description: Simon Says online free: watch four coloured pads light up, then repeat the pattern. Each round adds one step — how long can you keep up?
lede: The 1978 tabletop classic, in your browser. Four big coloured pads light up in a pattern, each with its own note, and your job is to play it back exactly. Round one is a single light. Every round adds one more step, and the pattern plays a little faster as it grows. One wrong pad and the pattern breaks — how many rounds can you repeat before it slips away?

p: Press Start watching and the pads begin. Green, red, yellow and blue light up one at a time, each with its own note, in a pattern you have to remember. When the pattern finishes, the message changes to your turn: tap the pads back in exactly the same order.

Get it right and a new step is added to the end of the pattern, so round two is two lights, round three is three, and so on. Tap a wrong pad and the game ends where you stand, with the number of rounds you repeated and a badge for your memory. Your best is saved on this device.

The first pattern is a single light, so everybody starts with a success. Each round adds exactly one step to the end, which means the pattern is never a surprise: you have already repeated everything except the newest light.

The pattern also plays a little faster as it grows. The first lights stay on for just over half a second; by the later rounds each light is closer to a third of a second. The gap between lights stays the same, so the rhythm is steady even when the notes come quicker.

Simon was released in 1978 by Milton Bradley, designed by Ralph Baer — the engineer behind the first home video game console — and Howard J. Morrison. The tabletop toy had four big coloured buttons, green, red, yellow and blue, each playing a different note, and it asked players to repeat the sequence it played. It was an instant hit: the first run sold out, and the toy has stayed in production in one form or another ever since.

The four notes here are the same ones the original used: green plays the highest note and blue the lowest. Psychologists later found the game is a neat test of short-term memory — most people can hold about seven steps comfortably, which is exactly where the pattern starts to feel hard. Reaching ten rounds means you are remembering more than most people can repeat after a single hearing.

ol: Say the colours out loud as they light up, or in your head: green, red, yellow. Hearing the pattern as words gives your memory a second way to hold it.
Watch the centre of the board, not the pad that is lighting up. You can see all four pads at once from the middle, and you will not lose the thread chasing the light.
Group the pattern into chunks of three or four, the way you remember a phone number. A twelve-step pattern is just three short groups.
Do not rush your turn. The pads wait for you, so take a breath, play the pattern back in your head, and then tap it out.
On a phone, hold the device steady and tap with your index finger. Big pads are forgiving, but a thumb stretched across the board is not.

p: For another memory test, flip the cards in [[memory-match]] and find every pair. If you would rather test your reflexes than your memory, see how fast you can tap in the [[reaction-time-test]]. You can find every old favourite in [[cat:classic|classic games]].

faq: How long is the first pattern?
One light. Round one is a single pad, round two adds a second light, and every round after that adds exactly one more step to the end of the pattern you already know.
Yes, a little. Each light stays on for just over half a second at first and closer to a third of a second in the later rounds. The gap between lights stays the same, so the rhythm is steady.
What happens if I tap the wrong pad?
The game ends at once. You keep the rounds you already repeated, and the results card shows your badge and your best score so far.
Can I play with the keyboard?
Yes. Keys 1 to 4 light up green, red, yellow and blue in order, and the arrow keys do the same: up for green, right for red, down for yellow and left for blue.
Yes. Your best number of rounds is saved in this browser on this device, and it is shown at the top of the screen and on the start card.
